newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BOBSLEIGH-WINNING SWISS DISQUALIFIED FOR ILLEGAL SLEDS.
newsitem.headline: BOBSLEIGH-WINNING SWISS DISQUALIFIED FOR ILLEGAL SLEDS.

text.p: Switzerland swept the top three places in the world four-man bobsleigh championship on Sunday but were then disqualified for using illegal equipment.
The Swiss Bobsleigh Federation immediately filed a protest which will be considered by the International Bobsleigh Federation within three weeks, most likely at the World Cup finals in Nagano, Japan.
Until then the order of finish will remain unchanged, meaning an anxious wait for the Swiss -- and German and United States crews placed fourth to sixth.

Reto Goetschi, who led Switzerland to victory in the two-man event last Sunday, continued to benefit from home-track advantage by posting the fastest time in the four-man as well. He finished ahead of sleds driven by Christian Reich and Marcel Rohner.
But, three hours after the Swiss had been awarded their medals, they were informed that during scrutineering all three sleds were found to have illegal axles -- a bar which joins the runners.
"We are sure the equipment is legal," said Martin Berthod, secretary of the Swiss federation. "They are all pretty much the same on all sleds."
